questions.problem:
Find the determinant of the matrix 
$N=[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ \sqrt{6} & -1 & 0 & 0 \\ 5 & 0 & \sqrt{5} & 2 \\ \sqrt{3} & 0 & 0 & \sqrt{5}\end{aligned}].$
questions.worked_solution:
Notice that the $1$st row contains three zeros. So, using Laplace expansion along the $1$st row, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{det}(N) & =|\begin{aligned}2 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ \sqrt{6} & -1 & 0 & 0 \\ 5 & 0 & \sqrt{5} & 2 \\ \sqrt{3} & 0 & 0 & \sqrt{5}\end{aligned}| \\  & =2\cdot (-1)^{1+1}|\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & \sqrt{5} & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & \sqrt{5}\end{aligned}| \\  & =2\cdot |\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & \sqrt{5} & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & \sqrt{5}\end{aligned}|\end{aligned}
$$

The determinant of a triangular matrix is equal to the product of the entries on the main diagonal. Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}2\cdot |\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & \sqrt{5} & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & \sqrt{5}\end{aligned}| & =2\cdot ((-1)\cdot \sqrt{5}\cdot \sqrt{5})=-10.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we obtain

$$
det(N)=-10.
$$

questions.problem:
Find the determinant of the matrix 
$B=[\begin{aligned}5 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 2 & 6 & 0 & 0 \\ -4 & 1 & 2 & 8 \\ 9 & 0 & 0 & -1\end{aligned}].$
questions.worked_solution:
Notice that the $3$rd column contains three zeros. So, using Laplace expansion along the $3$rd column, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}det(B) & =|\begin{aligned}5 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 2 & 6 & 0 & 0 \\ -4 & 1 & 2 & 8 \\ 9 & 0 & 0 & -1\end{aligned}| \\  & =2\cdot (-1)^{3+3}|\begin{aligned}5 & 0 & 0 \\ 2 & 6 & 0 \\ 9 & 0 & -1\end{aligned}| \\  & =2\cdot |\begin{aligned}5 & 0 & 0 \\ 2 & 6 & 0 \\ 9 & 0 & -1\end{aligned}|\end{aligned}
$$

The determinant of a triangular matrix is equal to the product of the entries on the main diagonal. Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}2\cdot |\begin{aligned}5 & 0 & 0 \\ 2 & 6 & 0 \\ 9 & 0 & -1\end{aligned}| & =2\cdot 5\cdot 6\cdot (-1)=-60.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we obtain

$$
det(B)=-60.
$$

questions.problem:
Given that $det({A}^{T})=7$, which of the following statements are true?

I. $3\text{det}(A)=21$

II. $-2\text{det}({A}^{T})=14$

III. $\text{det}(A)+2\text{det}(I)=9$
questions.worked_solution:
From the properties of determinants, we know that 

$$
\text{det}(A)=\text{det}({A}^{T})=7
$$

and

$$
det(I)=1.
$$

With that in mind, let's analyze each statement in turn.

- Statement I is true. Indeed,

$$
3\text{det}(A)=3\cdot 7=21.
$$

- Statement II is false. We have

$$
-2\text{det}({A}^{T})=-2\cdot 7=-14\ne 14.
$$

- Statement III is true. We have

$$
\text{det}(A)+2\text{det}(I)=7+2\cdot 1=9.
$$

In conclusion, the correct answer is "I and III only".

questions.problem:
Calculate the volume of the $4$-dimensional parallelepiped spanned by the vectors

$$
a=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -7 \\ 4 \\ -2\end{aligned}],\,b=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 3 \\ -1 \\ 8\end{aligned}],\,c=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0 \\ 4 \\ -11\end{aligned}],\,d=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0 \\ 0 \\ -2\end{aligned}].
$$
questions.worked_solution:
First, let's construct the matrix $M,$ whose columns are the coordinates of our vectors $a,$ $b,$ $c,$ and  $d:$

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}3 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ -7 & 3 & 0 & 0 \\ 4 & -1 & 4 & 0 \\ -2 & 8 & -11 & -2\end{aligned}]
$$

The volume of the parallelepiped spanned by these vectors equals the absolute value of the determinant of $M:$

$$
V=|det(M)|
$$

The determinant of a triangular matrix is equal to the product of the entries on the main diagonal. So, we have

$$
det(M)=[\begin{aligned}3 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ -7 & 3 & 0 & 0 \\ 4 & -1 & 4 & 0 \\ -2 & 8 & -11 & -2\end{aligned}]=3\cdot 3\cdot 4\cdot (-2)=-72.
$$

Therefore, the volume is

$$
V=|det(M)|=|-72|=72.
$$

questions.problem:
Calculate the volume of the $4$-dimensional parallelepiped spanned by the vectors

$$
a=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 0 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}],\,b=[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 4 \\ 4 \\ 0\end{aligned}],\,c=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0 \\ 3 \\ 0\end{aligned}],\,d=[\begin{aligned}7 \\ 1 \\ 6 \\ 5\end{aligned}].
$$
questions.worked_solution:
First, let's construct the matrix $M,$ whose columns are the coordinates of our vectors $a,$ $b,$ $c,$ and  $d:$

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}-2 & 5 & 0 & 7 \\ 0 & 4 & 0 & 1 \\ 1 & 4 & 3 & 6 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 5\end{aligned}]
$$

The volume of the parallelepiped spanned by these vectors equals the absolute value of the determinant of $M:$

$$
V=|det(M)|
$$

Notice that the $3$rd column of the determinant contains three zeros. So, using Laplace expansion along the $3$rd column, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}det(M) & =|\begin{aligned}-2 & 5 & 0 & 7 \\ 0 & 4 & 0 & 1 \\ 1 & 4 & 3 & 6 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 5\end{aligned}| \\  & =3\cdot (-1)^{3+3}|\begin{aligned}-2 & 5 & 7 \\ 0 & 4 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 5\end{aligned}| \\  & =3|\begin{aligned}-2 & 5 & 7 \\ 0 & 4 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 5\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

The determinant of a triangular matrix is equal to the product of the entries on the main diagonal. Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}det(M) & =3|\begin{aligned}-2 & 5 & 7 \\ 0 & 4 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 5\end{aligned}| \\  & =3\cdot (-2)\cdot 4\cdot 5 \\  & =-120\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the volume is

$$
V=|det(M)|=|-120|=120.
$$
